liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Franklin's Tower** (3 reviews): Franklin's is played at a ferocious tempo without sounding speeded up; Franklin's is fast but seems aimless and repetitive to this reviewer, not a highlight [18][20][21]
- **Stella Blue** (2 reviews): A long, lilting intro leads into a strong Stella Blue with standout Jerry playing; The Other One moves into Stella Blue with patience and smoothness rarely heard in later years [16][18]
- **Little Red Rooster** (2 reviews): Listener questions who plays the first solo before Bobby's in Little Red Rooster; The solo before Bobby's is a keyboard solo by Brent, not a guest guitarist [24][25]
- **The Other One** (1 review): Space leads out of drums into a heavy Other One, with Jerry and Phil making it a classic [16]
- **Let It Grow** (1 review): Very melodic playing from Jerry stands out in Let It Grow [18]
- **Estimated Prophet** (1 review): Named with Let It Grow, Samson and Stella Blue as highlights [20]
- **Deal** (1 review): Let It Grow into Deal has an end-jam peak, matched by next night's Deal in College Park [21]
- **Jack Straw** (1 review): Jerry plays strongly on the Jack Straw opener [26]

## Setlist highlights

- **gd81-03-06 s1 t01 Crowd**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [28]
- **gd81-03-06 s1 t02 Jack Straw**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [28]
- **gd81-03-06 s1 t03 Peggy O**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [28]
- **gd81-03-06 s1 t04 Cassidy**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [28]
- **gd81-03-06 s1 t05 They Love Each Other**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [28]
- **gd81-03-06 s1 t06 El Paso**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [28]
- **gd81-03-06 s1 t07 Row Jimmy**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [28]
- **gd81-03-06 s1 t08 Little Red Rooster**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [28]

## The recordings

- **gd1981-03-06.139741.fob.beyer.m160.streeter.miller.clugston.flac1644** (recommended): audience recording; 22 songs; 172 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [1]
- **gd1981-03-06.169229.nak700.wagner.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 20 songs; 185 min [3]
- **gd1981-03-06.169387.nak300.cm.ismokeweed.flac2448**: audience recording; 20 songs; 178 min [5]. Said about its sound: Pretty good recording with a quiet crowd; sound changed at the start of the second set [5]
- **gd1981-03-06.nak700.taylor-radnor.gross.gems.83827.flac16**: source not stated; 20 songs; 176 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [6]
- **gd81-03-06.wise.lutch.3921.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 20 songs; 175 min; rated 3.92/5 by 13 [10]. Said about its sound: Audience tape sounds fairly distant, with so-so audio quality [21]
- **gd81-03-06.set2-sbd.fink.14019.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 10 songs; 93 min; rated 4.5/5 by 2 [12]. Said about its sound: Soundboard is very clean though not the crispiest; Phil's bass bombs in the Roses come through well [16]

## Around the show

- Reviewer calls the theater one of the best places to see the Dead; the audience tape captures its atmosphere [17]
- Small intimate theater with velvet ropes; a fan-made sign outside carried the Dead's logo and a slogan [19]
- Phil played thirteen bass notes opening a song, which was much discussed after the show and next day in MD [22]
- Taper recorded under the balcony; crowd was quiet, and a security guard demanded money to record [5]
- The band drove through a blinding snowstorm to reach Pittsburgh [30]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1981-03-06.139741.fob.beyer.m160.streeter.miller.clugston.flac1644**: taped by Frank Streeter; transferred by Charlie Miller and Scott Clugston; source: Source Info: Frank Streeter's Master FOB Audience Cassette; Beyer M160 > Sony TC-D5M (Maxell MX90); Transfer Info: Cassette Master (Nakamichi CR-7A) > Tascam… [1]
- **gd1981-03-06.169229.nak700.wagner.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Bob Wagner; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Bob Wagner's Master Audience Cassettes; Nakamichi 700 mics > Sony TC-D5M (Maxell XLII-S90) [3]
- **gd1981-03-06.169387.nak300.cm.ismokeweed.flac2448**: taped by ismokeweed; transferred by ismokeweed; source: this is a digital copy of a master stereo audience recording made with 2xnak300 mics into a sony tcd5m. [5]
- **gd1981-03-06.nak700.taylor-radnor.gross.gems.83827.flac16**: taped by Mason Taylor and Mark Radnor; transferred by Todd Evans and Jamie Waddell; source: NAK 700 (shotgun capsules) > Nak 550 Cassette Recorder > Maxell Metal > HHB Porta-a-DAT [6]. Also: Nakamichi 700 recording by Taylor and Radnor; set one tuning and encore supplied from Jim Wise's tape [6]
- **gd81-03-06.wise.lutch.3921.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Jim Wise; transferred by Jim Wise; source: Audience Recording: Sennheiser 421>D5 set up loge center [10]
- **gd81-03-06.set2-sbd.fink.14019.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [12]

## Art and photos
